- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.33) — model misses downward momentum or fails to adjust for bearish signals.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast remains high for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean; true price tends to revert toward 3–5 day average after spikes.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 1–3% in bullish sentiment periods, underestimate in bearish or neutral sentiment.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — model replicates sentiment direction without adjusting for historical price behavior or volatility clustering.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often assumes continuation — but true price often peaks and reverses within 5–7 days.
